THE DESIGN JUDGMENT

Move the commitment earlier.
Keep the consequence.

The problem was the purchase threshold: players could afford neither function until the early opportunities had gone. More supplies would hide that problem.

The supply constraint stays fixed
Start with 3. Every valid action ends with +1; all sessions last 6 turns. Both builds together still cost 6. People and routes are outcomes, not supply income.
01
Split the purchase, not the total price

Replace one 6-supply purchase with 3 + 3. Each part has a usable function immediately. Full construction needs one extra action.

02
Make the first choice depend on the goal

An early signal saves 6 people. An early survey marks 3 routes. A different assignment changes which opening is useful.

03
Explain the window before the click

The transport boat leaves and the tide rises after turn 2. You can preserve one early opportunity, not both. Later action still helps, but gives less.

The opening matters to this assignment

Survey kit first meets this assignment. The other modular opening loses the early opportunity it did not prepare for. No legal route gets both early rewards.

What we accept in exchange

One more build action. Two mid-session waits on these completed routes. More information to understand before the first click; a wrong opening cannot recover the early window.
